annotation.authors_or_issuer: Minister of Works and Transport (Uganda); Uganda Civil Aviation Authority
key_provisions_or_claims: Three risk-based operation categories (basic, standard, complex) with escalating approval, licensing and documentation requirements
Mandatory registration of all UAS, ownership eligibility rules, and approval for import, export and manufacture
UAS Operator Certificate, remote pilot licence/authorisation, safety management system and third-party insurance for categories B and C
BVLOS requires detect-and-avoid and authority approval; highly automated operations need prior authorisation
Privacy, security vetting, interception powers and penalties up to 100 currency points or three years' imprisonment
annotation.summary_en: Uganda's Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2022 set a risk-based regime for drones. They cover registration, operator certification, pilot licensing, operating rules, BVLOS and automated operations, insurance, security vetting, privacy, interception powers and penalties. They revoke the 2020 RPAS Regulations.
